> Wow! You pretty much rewrote most of the code in 24 hours. Testing it and it works really well. A couple of questions.
> 
> 1. Why did it have to go to a single entry?  I'm assuming it has to do with how you've made it set the brightness mode and the effects list.

Since there was a custom effect list per device, it seemed too complex to try to manage that with a single config entry.

Also it allows us to use the built-in retry logic when the device is offline or the ip changes (`updates` here will cause the config entry to automatically reload with the new ip address when discovery detects it via dhcp or the `flux_led` discovery -- https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/56354/files#diff-b632edd25f6429e2a447af1ae9af6c7658f57135d7a19ef1ec9bb677780b2f5cR111).

Finally, we don't have to worry about the device registry or entity registry since removing the config entry will clean it up automatically.

> 2. I had made several updates and tired to have a PR accepted but, @emontnemery thought was too big and request to have the scope narrowed and the updates done in stages.  Has this gotten too big again since it's more than the config flow @emontnemery ?

Its a bit larger than I would have liked, but the integration looks like it hasn't had a code owner in a while so it needed a lot more love than I was expecting when I really got into the cleanup.  Its got 100% coverage now so it should be lower risk to merge the changes now.

I tried to define manually each bulb, but no better result

MagicHome bulb

comments:
How many bulbs?

Can you run "flux_led -sSti" on the command line and paste what comes back?

Yeah, there's lots of people complaining on forums about `flux_led` not assigning unique ids. 

It's a problem for me because you can't configure entities and assign them to an area unless they have a unique_id.

I also request the ability to add a unique_id to each - even if manually added ie:

```
light:
  - platform: flux_led
    devices:
      192.168.1.81:
        name: String LEDs
        mode: "rgb"
        unique_id: “Magic_LED_1”
```

Can this be added?

Thanks.

+1 to being able to specify a unique ID, even if it must be done manually.
Unfortunately the new lamps with the LEDENET protocol do not surprise tasmota or ESPHome like the ones before.
